newsitem.title: JAPAN: US T-bond price softer in Tokyo after losses in NY.
newsitem.headline: US T-bond price softer in Tokyo after losses in NY.

text.p: The key 30-year U.S. Treasury bond price softened in morning trade on Monday due to follow-through sales after heavy losses on Friday following the release of surprisingly strong U.S. economic data, dealers said.
The dollar's retreat from Friday's high of around 119.10 yen and concerns about fresh supply due to quarterly refunding this week also weighed on prices, they added.

"The price was a bit easier due to continued liquidation of longs built up before the economic data," said a brokerage dealer. The 30-year bond due 2027 stood at 102-05/32 at 0213 GMT, yielding 6.46 percent, down from 102-09/32 in New York.
The key 30-year U.S. bond yield ended at 6.45 percent in New York on Friday.
Dealers said the U.S. jobs report for July and the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) data may have dented the market's bullish sentiment.
"There was a change in the attitudes of market participants who were unanimously bullish," said the brokerage dealer.
"People had thought that even though production activity rose, inflation would be kept under control. But Friday's data raised doubts about whether such thinking would be correct," he added.
